title: Serve Economics CTA experiments
content:
Purpose:
- Combine competitive analysis + tested microcopy to produce 6 distinct CTA and tagline variants for the main marketing funnel (top-of-site hero + product pages for Dedicated/Private).
- Pick 2–3 variants to A/B and measure activation, pricing inquiries, and demo requests.

Context / hypothesis notes (TL;DR):
- Our wins are performance predictability, cost controls, and deployment flexibility. Customers care less about raw model magic and more about predictable per-request economics and fallback guarantees.
- Competitors emphasize simplicity or scale; we should emphasize: predictable unit economics, seamless fallbacks, and engineering-grade controls.
- We need CTAs that map to distinct buyer intents: quick trial (self-serve), capacity conversation (dedicated), security conversation (private/enterprise).

Audience segments to address (quick sketches):
- Platform engineers: prioritize latency SLOs, predictable p99, network isolation options.
- ML engineers/ML infra: want batching, quantization guidance, cost per token tradeoffs.
- Product + PMs at scale-ups: care about cost per active user and reliability of chat features.
- Security/compliance buyers: need VPC/on-prem options, KMS, audit logs, SOC2.

Competitive snapshot (notes + implications):
- Vendor A: strong model catalogue and simplicity; messaging leans on "just call our API". Implication: we should NOT only pitch ease; differentiate on economics + controls.
- Vendor B: enterprise SAP/financial focus with lots of compliance copy. Implication: Private page needs concrete checklist items (KMS, HSM, audit retention numbers).
- Vendor C: low-cost quantized hosting play; messaging on price per token. Implication: align our Optimize toolkit copy to call out tooling that *reduces* cost without headcount.

Key claims (short bullets we want on page):
- Predictable per-request economics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- SLA-backed latency tiers and automated fallbacks to keep production live.
- Platform-first tooling: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations tailored to your workload.
- Pin and rollout model versions with canary/A-B controls and telemetry.

Proof points / evidence to use inline:
- Internal bench: 35% median token-cost reduction on customer workloads after Optimize recommendations (anonymized).
- SLA example: 99.95% availability for Dedicated customers on standard tier (internal doc ref).
- Case anecdote: "reduced inference spend 40% while improving p99 by 20%" — early customer quote to request from SE.

Objections & rebuttals (short):
- "We can host cheaper ourselves" -> "Possibly, but total cost of ownership includes SRE time, model-ops, and mitigation for latency tails; Redwood reduces operational overhead and gives predictable unit economics + tooling."
- "Vendor lock-in concerns" -> "Open model support, model pinning, and exportable configs; optional private deployments keep data/control in your environment."

Landing headline / tagline candidates (6 variants) – try to be distinct in tone and hook. Keep as short lines for A/B: 
1) Fidelity you can measure. Cost you can control.
2) Ship LLM features with production predictability.
3) Predictable inference for real products (not experiments).
4) Fast, reliable, and cost-aware LLM serving for engineers.
5) Keep latency low, costs transparent, and control in your stack.
6) Stop guessing at inference economics — measure, optimize, serve.

Subhead / 1-line followups (examples paired to taglines):
- For 1: "Transparent per-request metrics, workload-aware batching, and SLA-backed capacity."
- For 2: "Hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployments with the same developer experience."
- For 3: "From pilot to scale with rollout policies, tracing, and cost tools."

Primary CTA matrix (map CTA to audience intent):
- Try for free (self-serve onboarding + credit) -> target: developer/ML engineer.
- Request capacity estimate -> target: platform/infra + finance leads.
- Talk to solutions (demo + security questionnaire) -> target: security/compliance / enterprise buyers.
- Calculate your savings -> interactive micro-tool leading to demo or signup (engagement).

CTA text candidates (short list to test):
- Start free (lowest friction)
- Run a cost check (interactive)
- Estimate dedicated capacity
- Request an enterprise demo
- See latency SLOs

Microcopy for the CTA area (variants):
- "Start free — 1000 inference credits, no card required."
- "Estimate savings on your workload — upload a sample trace or paste token velocity."
- "Schedule a 15-minute capacity review with a solutions engineer."
- "Get our SOC2 + compliance checklist for private deployments."

Primary page sections (suggested order):
- Above the fold (tagline + subhead + 2 CTAs + social proof line)
- How it works (runtime, routing, caching, quantization) — short bullets + single-line proof points
- Which deployment is right for you (hosted / dedicated / private) — 3-column microcopy with CTA per column
- Cost & performance guardrails (Optimize toolkit highlights; interactive calculator link)
- Reliability & fallback story (routing policies, canary rollback, SLA summary)
- Security & compliance (for private deployments: KMS, logging, on-prem)
- Customers + benchmarks (blinded numbers)
- FAQ + objection handling (short Qs + links to docs)

Product-page copy snippets (Dedicated & Private)
- Dedicated (headline)
  "Guaranteed throughput, isolated capacity."
  Bullets: "Reserve GPU pools; Autoscale with bursts; SLA-backed latency tiers; Per-route cost buckets."
- Dedicated (CTA microcopy)
  "Estimate committed capacity" / "Talk to sales about a pilot"

- Private (headline)
  "Inference inside your network — full control, enterprise-grade governance."
  Bullets: "Customer-managed control plane; Optional on-prem package; KMS/HSM integrations; Audit retention controls."
- Private (CTA microcopy)
  "Get the compliance pack" / "Schedule a private deployment consult"

Competitive differentiators to call out on product pages (short checklist we can iconify):
- Unified API across deployment modes
- Latency/backpressure routing + automatic fallback to compatible variants
- Transparent per-token economics and token-level tracing
- Built-in quality regression alerts tied to eval sets

Measurement plan / success metrics for the test: 
- Primary: signups that convert to active API key usage within 14 days (activation rate).
- Secondary: Estimated demo requests from enterprise CTAs; time-to-demo; and # of cost-check tool runs.
- Qualitative: CS feedback on demo leads; sales objections logged.
- Statistical plan: run each headline x CTA variant for ~2 weeks or 10k uniques per cell. Track binomial conversion and use Bayesian stopping rule after 10k visitors.

Implementation notes for engineering / growth: 
- Experiment IDs: page copy experiments should append ?exp=serve-econ-v{n} for tracing in GA + Segment.
- Server-side flags exist in github PR-834 — coordinate with webops (ENG-4219) to toggle variants.
- Analytics events required: hero_cta_click, cost_tool_launch, demo_request_submit with property: audience_intent.

Open questions / items to collect before launch: 
- Do we have permission to publish the 35% median token-cost reduction claim? Legal/Research sign-off required. (Who owns: Research -> Marta)
- Customer quote for the "reduced inference spend 40%" anecdote — ask SEs for permission to anonymize.
- Build scope for the interactive savings calculator: MVP will accept token rate + monthly queries and return estimated $/month. Engineering estimate needed (point to ENG-4331).

Next steps (practical):
1) Pick top 3 taglines from the list (product + growth sync on Monday)
2) Finalize CTA mapping and microcopy; hand to webops for experiment wiring (ENG-4219)
3) Legal & Research signoff on quantitative claims
4) Wireframe the cost calculator and backlog a mini-epic (ENG-4331)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a small banner on Dedicated product page: "Ask about committed spot pools" — some customers prefer committing to spot-equivalent price.
- For Private: link to a downloadable checklist (PDF) that lists regulatory controls and deployment options. Quick win for gating demo conversations.

Slack refs / tickets / owners:
- Growth thread: #growth-homepage-test (ask Liam to pin top variants)
- SE request: chime in with a customer quote (owner: Jordan Lee)
- Legal: legal@redwood (note for claims)

Rough copy artifacts for immediate paste into CMS (pick-first drafts):
- Tagline A: "Ship LLM features with production predictability."
  Subhead: "Transparent per-request economics, SLA-backed capacity, and the tools engineers need to scale."
  CTA-1: "Start free" (secondary: "Estimate savings")

- Tagline B: "Stop guessing at inference economics — measure, optimize, serve."
  Subhead: "Workload-aware batching, KV caching, and cost recommendations to make inference economical at scale."
  CTA-1: "Run a cost check" (secondary: "Request a demo")

- Tagline C (enterprise tone): "Inference inside your network with enterprise SLAs."
  Subhead: "Private and dedicated deployment options, audit logs, and key management integrations."
  CTA-1: "Request a secure consult" (secondary: "Get compliance pack")

End notes: this doc is intentionally broad — prefer tests that isolate the headline from CTA (multivariate noise). Avoid combining major layout changes with copy tests in early rounds.

-- Priya
